title: Naming squares fast, from either side
outcomes: Names a square pointed at on either side of the board without counting from the edge
Uses the square colour as a quick check on a name
Does not mirror squares when the board is turned

steps.text: In **The board and its square names** you learned that a square is its file letter, then its rank number. Now the aim is speed. Two habits replace counting. First, read the letter and number along the board's edge. Second, check the **colour**: a1 is dark, and a square is dark when its letter's place in the alphabet plus its rank number is even (a=1, b=2). This holds on every square.

steps.caption: The bishop on a1 reaches only dark squares: b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7, h8. Check: d is the 4th letter and the rank is 4, 4+4=8, even.

line.say: The bishop slides to d4. It stays on dark squares: 4+4=8 is even.

steps.text: A real board has no letters on it, and this app's board turns to Black's side. The names stay with the squares, so only the picture changes. The common slip is to **mirror**: reading the square on screen as if White were looking, so b3 becomes g6. As a **rule of thumb**, find the letter on the edge first, then the number, and never copy the picture.

steps.title: One square, three ways of reading it
steps.prompt: The same white rook seen from White's side, seen from Black's side, and read by copying the picture as if White were looking. Predict first: which readings name the rook's square correctly?

steps.text: Limits of these checks. The colour test tells you a name is wrong, not which name is right: two dark squares both pass. The edge-letter habit needs letters on the board; on a real board learn the corners instead: a1 is dark at White's left, h1 is light at White's right (8+1=9 is odd). Both are **rules of thumb** for speed, so keep practising until naming is automatic.

steps.prompt: How sure are you that you can name any square pointed at, from either side, without counting? Which kind (a far corner, Black's side, a crowded middle) was slowest? (low / medium / high)
